Commentary.Commentary: Welcome back for the second essay. The two umpires head out to the centre and they are joined by the Afghanistan players. It will be the left-hand right-hand combination of Tony de Zorzi and Temba Bavuma to open the innings for South Africa. With no Fazalhaq Farooqi in the side in this game, who will it be to start things off for Afghanistan? It is going to be the right-arm seamer, Naveed Zadran. Let's play...
... THE RUN CHASE ...

South Africa’s bowlers were in complete control from the start, applying relentless pressure that left Afghanistan searching for answers. With a modest target of 170 runs in 50 overs, South Africa appear well-positioned to end the series with a win, especially with the absence of Afghanistan's star bowler Rashid Khan. Can Afghanistan pull off a remarkable defence, or will South Africa cruise to a comfortable victory? Stay tuned to find out.

Afghanistan's head coach, Jonathan Trott is in for a chat. He says that before the game, he was happier than he is right now. Trott feels they have lacked in decision-making with their running between the wickets and are a few runs short. He believes that playing three games in five days serves as good practice for the Champions Trophy where there is going to be a similar gap between games. Adds that even one loss in that event could potentially knock the team out and it is important to stay on top of the game always.

AM Ghazanfar provided some resistance toward the end, managing to push Afghanistan to a somewhat respectable total. However, the innings was marred by a series of run-outs, caused by poor communication between batters, which stunted their progress.

Afghanistan have been bundled out for a mere 169 runs by an outstanding display with the ball and in the field by South Africa. Temba Bavuma and his men have been on top of their game from the start of the innings and have given themselves a very good chance to win the third ODI. Despite a valiant effort from Rahmanullah Gurbaz, who scored a fighting 89 at the top, the rest of Afghanistan's batting lineup struggled to get going. Gurbaz, fresh off a century in the previous game, was the lone bright spot, but his effort wasn’t enough to steer Afghanistan to a competitive total.

Hits it flat and straight to long on where Aiden Markram leaps and takes it over his head. Peter ends with two wickets to his name. Afghanistan have been bowled out for 169.

A confident shout for caught behind but the umpire is unmoved! There was a noise as the ball went past the bat and this time, South Africa take the review. Fortuin stays around the wicket and tosses it up nicely, full and outside off, Mohammad Nabi presses forward to defend it with a straight bat. He fails to get to the pitch of the ball and it spins away to go past the outside edge. The UltraEdge shows a spike when the ball is next to the bat and the on-field decision will have to be overturned. OUT! RUN OUT! Would you believe it? Third run out of the inning. Ikram Alikhil took it casually and paid the ultimate price. Markram drops it short from around the wicket, slower as well, on middle and leg, Rahmanullah Gurbaz shapes up for the pull but goes through his shot early and toe-ends the shot to the left of mid-wicket. Gurbaz initially takes a couple of steps for the run and seeing that, Ikram Alikhil sets off too. Gurbaz sends him back and Ikram retreats but he does not expect the diving Temba Bavuma to release the throw. Bavuma dives and picks the ball cleanly before having a shy at the bowling end and since Ikram is a bit lazy to return, he is struggling to make his ground. Commentary.Commentary: Drinks break! Compared to the second ODI, this has been a stronger start for South Africa. They've focused on attacking the stumps more effectively, and although a couple of dismissals have come through run outs, their bowling kept the Afghan batters quiet during the Powerplay. Rahmanullah Gurbaz, however, has picked up right where he left off in the last game and will be eager to convert this start into yet another three-figure score. As we saw in the second ODI, batting under lights proved challenging for the Proteas against the Afghan spinners and to limit Afghanistan to a manageable total, South Africa will need to continue chipping away at the wickets. Azmatullah Omarzai joins Gurbaz out in the middle.

OUT! RUN OUT! Excellent throw from the deep by Tristan Stubbs! Aiden Markram drops it short outside the off stump. Hashmatullah Shahidi slaps it to the right of sweeper covers and sets off for a quick couple. Tristan Stubbs picks up the ball at once and makes a brilliant throw, flat and on the bounce, next to the stumps at the batting end. The keeper, Kyle Verreynne barely has to move and he does the rest by disturbing the stumps. Hashmatullah Shahidi looks in trouble as the umpires refer the run-out decision upstairs. The replays show that Hashmatullah Shahidi is short of his crease and Afghanistan lose another wicket. Afghanistan are now 74/3 after 15.1 overs.

OUT! LBW! The slower ball has done the trick for Lungi Ngidi! Or has it? The debutant, Abdul Malik walks up to his partner and after a chat, he takes the review. Ngidi cleverly rolls his fingers over the ball and attacks the stumps, bowls it on a length, on middle. Abdul Malik gets on the front foot and tries to play it across the line. Plays all around it as the ball comes back in to beat the inside edge. Abdul gets rapped on the front pad, right in front of the stumps. South Africa go up in unison and the finger is raised. There is no bat involved on UltraEdge and it is three reds on Ball Tracking. South Africa have their first breakthrough. Abdul, on ODI debut, goes for 9 (19) and Afghanistan are now 27/1 after 6.3 overs.

Commentary.Commentary: We are all set for the action to start. The two umpires make their way out to the middle, followed by Temba Bavuma and his men. Rahmanullah Gurbaz will have a new opening partner in the form of the debutant, Abdul Malik. Lungi Ngidi will start with the new ball for South Africa. Away we go!

PITCH REPORT - Niall O'Brien is near the deck. He starts by saying that it's another hot day in Sharjah with temperatures soaring to 38 degrees, and the lack of wind makes for taxing conditions. Tells that we are on pitch number 2, which is hard and true. Further says that there won't be a great deal of bounce, but a bit of turn will be on offer. Vernon Philander joins him and says that it will be crucial to bring the stumps into play. Adds that from South Africa's perspective, they haven't been able to do that effectively.

The captain of South Africa, Temba Bavuma says that the wicket became much drier in the second innings of the second game. He says that they have to perform well with the ball, calling it their first assignment, and shares that the talk has been about hitting the stumps more. Bavuma admits that they expected tough conditions, and says that the players unfamiliar with these environments have now gotten a proper sense of what to expect. He believes that going forward, they will have a better understanding of how to succeed here. Informs that Nandre Burger misses out and Andile Phehlukwayo comes in.

Afghanistan's captain Hashmatullah Shahidi expresses confidence ahead of the final match, stating that his team wants to bat first, as batting in the daytime has proven easier. He emphasizes that they aim to put South Africa under pressure by setting a solid total. Shahidi is elated with the series win, calling it a significant achievement for Afghanistan. He notes the unwavering support from fans back home and aims to carry the winning momentum into this game. Informs that they have made three changes with Abdul Malik, Fareed Ahmad and Naveed Zadran coming in for Riaz Hassan, Fazalhaq Farooqi and Rashid Khan respectively.

South Africa (Playing XI) - Temba Bavuma (C), Tony de Zorzi, Reeza Hendricks, Aiden Markram, Tristan Stubbs, Kyle Verreynne (WK), Wiaan Mulder, Andile Phehlukwayo (In for Nandre Burger), Bjorn Fortuin, Nqabayomzi Peter, Lungi Ngidi.

Afghanistan (Playing XI) - Rahmanullah Gurbaz, Abdul Malik (On debut) (In for Riaz Hassan), Rahmat Shah, Hashmatullah Shahidi (C), Azmatullah Omarzai, Ikram Alikhil (WK), Mohammad Nabi, Nangeyalia Kharote, AM Ghazanfar, Fareed Ahmad (In for Fazalhaq Farooqi), Naveed Zadran (In for Rashid Khan).
TOSS - Afghanistan have won the toss and have opted to BAT first.

The Kiwis have just lost Glenn Phillips, but Rachin Ravindra is standing firm, now joined by Mitchell Santner. With 104 runs still needed and only 4 wickets in hand, it's shaping up to be a gripping finale. Stay tuned for the toss and all the action here, but don’t miss out on the drama over there!

As we head into the final match of the series, Afghanistan will be eager to continue their dominant run, while South Africa will hope to turn things around and salvage some pride. Stick around for the toss and team news.

In contrast, South Africa's batting faltered once again. Chasing 311, they crumbled under the pressure, with only Temba Bavuma offering any real resistance. The Afghan bowling attack, led by Rashid Khan’s five-wicket haul and Nangeyalia Kharote’s four wickets, tore through the South African batting line-up, limiting them to just 134 runs. Afghanistan sealed a massive 177-run victory, underscoring their dominance in all facets of the game.

In the second ODI, Afghanistan's batting line-up set the tone for their dominant victory, posting an imposing total of 311 runs. Leading the charge was Rahmanullah Gurbaz, who scored a brilliant century, supported by Azmatullah Omarzai’s explosive 86 off just 50 balls. Their combined efforts gave Afghanistan a platform too difficult for South Africa to counter.

A warm welcome to everyone joining us for the third and final ODI between Afghanistan and South Africa at the iconic Sharjah Cricket Stadium. After a stunning series of performances, Afghanistan enter this match with a commanding 2-0 lead, having already secured the series win. With pride and momentum on their side, Afghanistan will be looking to complete a clean sweep, while South Africa will aim to salvage some respect in this encounter.
... MATCH DAY ...

Afghanistan and their fairytale affair with white-ball cricket continues as they face South Africa in the third and final ODI in Sharjah. After a fine showing in the ODI World Cup last year and reaching the T20 World Cup semifinal this year, Afghanistan have now taken an unassailable 2-0 lead in the three-match series. The Hashmatullah Shahidi-led side have blown away a Proteas side that is missing a few big names but still has enough talent and experience to perform at a high level. The Afghans have been relentless with the ball so far, bundling out South Africa for just over 100 runs in both ODIs and Rashid Khan has really enjoyed his time back after the T20 World Cup. However, they were prolific with the bat as well and amassed well over 300 runs in the previous game riding on the back of a century from Rahmanullah Gurbaz and a fiery 80-odd knock from Azmatullah Omarzai. On the other hand, South Africa might be missing a few big names but even the likes of Aiden Markram and Reeza Hendricks have struggled so far and the batting has been in utter shambles. They will be itching to turn things around in this final match and save a bit of face. Skipper, Temba Bavuma returned for the second game and the top order looked in decent nick but chasing over 300 runs, soon the Proteas started to crumble and could amass only 134 runs in total. They really need to improve their technique of playing as Sharjah isn't that difficult of a surface to bat on in general. The bowling too was under-par in the last game with only Lungi Ngidi showing some consistency from the previous game. Afghanistan on the other hand have found some really good rhythm with the ball and have really dominated proceedings with Fazalhaq Farooqi leading the pace attack really well. Azmatullah Omarzai has grown in stature as an all-rounder and is enjoying a purple patch, especially with the bat. Can South Africa manage to regroup and find their best form to finish the tour off on a winning note? Or will Afghanistan romp to a 3-0 series win? We shall find out.
